summary: A map created using imagery captured by a NASA space probe, the Odyssey. This map was designed to assist astronauts on Mars by identifying safe and unsafe areas for them to visit. It incorporates data sourced from NASA, including optical, thermal, spectral, topographical, geophysical, atmospheric, radiation, and chemical information.
details:
Project Name
Mars Mission: Survival Map

High-Level Project Summary
Mars Mission: Survival Map is an interactive web atlas that helps future explorers judge where to land and move safely on Mars. It combines eight layers of NASA data for Ares Vallis into a simple green and red safety map. An astronaut guide explains the results.

Detailed Project Description
Mars Mission: Survival Map is an interactive web guide built around Ares Vallis, one of the largest outflow channels on Mars. It stretches about 1,600 to 2,000 km, from the highlands of Margaritifer Terra to the plains of Chryse Planitia.

The site has four screens:

  1. A landing page with a GO button.
  2. An introduction to Ares Vallis.
  3. A multilayer atlas on a Mars Odyssey (THEMIS) base image (about 100 m/pixel). It overlays eight data layers: topography, temperature, spectral data, optical imagery, geophysics, atmosphere, radiation and surface chemistry.
  4. A “safezone map” that turns the data into a safety overlay.

On the safezone map:

  • Green areas are flatter regions with fewer obstacles. They make landing and astronaut movement easier and lower the risk of accidents.
  • Red areas have craters, slopes and uneven terrain. They need caution.

A friendly astronaut guide explains the map in plain language, so students and the general public can understand it. Its conclusion is that green areas are only potential candidates for exploration. No region is completely safe without detailed studies.

We built it to turn complex planetary data into something anyone can read at a glance. It supports the idea that careful site selection is the first step of survival on another planet.

NASA Data

  • Mars Odyssey THEMIS (base imagery, thermal, optical)
  • Mars Global Surveyor MOLA (topography)
  • Mars Global Surveyor (geophysical layer)
  • Mars Climate Sounder, MCS (atmosphere)
  • MARIE (radiation)
  • CRISM (spectral and chemical)
  • Gamma Ray Spectrometer, GRS (chemistry)
  • NASA Planetary Data System (PDS)
